messages.content:
<document id=DOC_req_years_nine_to_five>
Required: between 9 and 5 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_states_seven>
Backend engineering: 7 years building transactional services, most
recently a settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day.
</document>

Assess the candidate summary above against the posting requirement and say
whether the candidate matches it.

Let us discuss any ambiguities or mistakes in the requirement before
proceeding with the assessment.

response.text:
The requirement looks mistaken as written, so I would not score the candidate against it yet.

**“between 9 and 5 years”** is reversed. In ordinary usage the lower bound comes first (“between 5 and 9”). The interval is the same either way only if both numbers are meant as the endpoints of one range. It could also be a typo for “at least 5,” “at least 9,” “5 to 9,” or something else.

**“Between” is also unclear about the endpoints.** It may or may not include exactly 5 and exactly 9. That does not change a 7-year reading if the intended window really is 5–9, but it does matter if either endpoint was the real cutoff.

How should that line be read before any match decision: 5–9 inclusive, 5–9 exclusive, a minimum of 5, a minimum of 9, or a different intended range?
